Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Ross & Barry no Mairi & John, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr? In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts a quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams winning are the Pretenders, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Seumas and Mairi or Ceit and Eilidh, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Seumas & Mairi no Ceit & Eilidh, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr? In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Garradh Phadruig
programme.desc: Summer is over, but Peter is already preparing for the next growing season. Tha’n samhradh seachad ach tha Pàdruig a’deasachadh airson ràithe fàs na h-ath-bhliadhna.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Mhoireasdan, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. Actress-turned-interior designer, Erica Morrison, takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers, she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Tuath Cheòl le Ruairidh Gray
programme.desc: An seinneadair Ruairidh Gray a’ tadhal air an Grand Ole Opry ann an Glaschu agus a’ toirt sùil bhlàth air ais air sreathan Tuath Cheòl. Bidh Ruairidh a’ taghadh cuid de na taisbeanaidhean a bha anns na prògraman agus a bha a’ còrdadh gu mòr ri luchd-leantainn ceòl dùthchasach aig an àm. Am measg na bhios anns a’ phrògram seo, Na h-Òganaich, Anna Latharna NicIllÌosa, Murdigan Dòmhnallach, Màiri NicAonghais, Tormod MacIllEathain nach maireann, Iain Costello & Iain Moireach agus Fiona Cheanadach. Singer Ruairidh Gray visits Glasgow’s Grand Ole Opry for a nostalgic look back at the legendary music series Tuath Cheòl and presents musical selections from the original programmes. Hugely popular with country music fans at the time, this episode features musicians and singers including Na h-Òganaich, Anne Lorne Gillies, Murdigan MacDonald, Mairi MacInnes, Ian Costello & John Murray and Fiona Kennedy. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: An caladh na theine san t-seachdain mu dheireadh de sheusan a’ ghiomaich. Gun an còrr aige ri chall, tha Adam a’ cur a cheann an geall air an tùna. A fire rips through the harbour in the final week of lobster season. With little left to lose, Adam bets it all on tuna. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke forage at the shore for razor clams, kelp lasagne and carrageen dessert.

programme.title: Peat & Diesel
programme.desc: While a tour zig zagging the UK and Ireland pulls in the fans, the toll of being constantly on the road brings challenges for the Peat & Diesel boys.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le taisbeanadh air leth bho Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House aig Belladrum 2025 is an còmhlan cliùiteach Albannach, Texas, a’ tilleadh chun na fèise mar phrìomh chòmhlan oidhche Shathairne. Le fuaim leantaileach is guth iongantach Sharleen Spiteri, tha an còmhlan a’ toirt thugainn na h-òrain as fheàrr aca, ’s chan eil leisg air an t-sluagh seinn còmhla riutha. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain MacDonald present from the Hot House Stage at Belladrum as iconic Scottish band Texas return to the festival to headline Saturday night. With their timeless sound and Sharleen Spiteri’s unmistakable vocals, the group perform classic hits, and the crowd need no encouragement to join in.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: A pride of lions has rewritten the rules - they have learnt to take down elephants.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: Mammals have proved to be one of the most adaptable products of evolution. David Attenborough looks at their evolution from reptiles 200 million years ago. This remarkable transition involved the development of mechanisms for regulating body temperature, for allowing the young to develop in the womb and for suckling newborns. Attenborough also explores the South American origins of marsupials and their colonisation of Australia.

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose tells the story of the USS Squalus submarine which became stranded on the bottom of the Atlantic in 1939. No-one had ever been saved from a stricken sub beneath the ocean before, but maverick designer Charles Momsen, who had been ignored by the navy top brass, was suddenly called into action to bring up the crew. Rose meets the last living survivor from the sub and one of the men, now 103, who helped save him. The rescue kick-started a whole new era of technology, laying the foundation for modern deep-sea diving.

programme.title: Kabul
programme.desc: As the Taliban seize control of Kabul, chaos erupts. Zahara, a prosecutor, flees with her husband Baqir to the French embassy - the last one still open - where Gilles, the security chief, oversees the evacuation of diplomats, while refugees begin to gather. Fazal, Zahara’s son and a soldier in the Afghan National Army, watches as his unit deserts and decides to escape to the Panjshir, where resistance forces are forming. His sister, Amina, remains at Kabul’s hospital, caring for Nooria, a young girl who has just undergone surgery, as the Taliban approach. Meanwhile, Giovanni, an Italian diplomat, is suddenly promoted to consul after his ambassador flees, and Vera, a German intelligence officer, fights to return to Kabul to rescue General Hassan, the man who once saved her life.

programme.title: Kabul
programme.desc: Outside the French embassy, refugees wait anxiously as the Taliban begin to surround the area. Zahara, still on the run, hopes to find safety, while Gilles struggles to organise the evacuation of the growing number of refugees. Fazal, now being hunted by the Taliban, returns to Kabul to seek refuge with Martin, a former American intelligence contact. Amina witnesses the Taliban’s brutality toward Nooria and hesitates about whether to flee to the French embassy. Giovanni, dealing with the dire sanitary conditions at the airport, attempts to maintain order. Meanwhile, Vera sets off on her unauthorised mission to locate General Hassan.

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Audrey moves out of Grantleigh Manor. Her hopes of seeing the estate run along old lines are dashed when she discovers the new owner's background.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Richard is far from happy when Hyacinth concocts an elaborate plan to turn him into a Frosticle executive with the help of a chukka of golf!

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: It is said that the average woman gets through around 30 hairstyles in a lifetime, with some changing their look entirely every 15 months. Timeshift takes a loving and sometimes horrified look back at the iconic hairdos and 'must have' haircuts that both men and women in Britain have flirted with over the past 60 years. And it's some journey... from the meringue-like confections of Raymond 'Teasy Weasy' via the geometric 'bob' cuts of Vidal Sassoon, stopping off to take in the 'big hair' heyday of bouffants and beehives, and not forgetting the mullet, the feather cut and the ultimate 'bad hair day' look of 1970s perms. Our hair is the one part of our identity we can change in an instant and which speaks volumes about who we are, where we've come from and where we're going. Today, young women are revisiting hair fashions of an earlier generation - big hair and blowdrying are back in demand, whilst many young men sport Edwardian 'peaky blinder' short back and sides. Narrated by Wayne Hemingway.

programme.title: Tech Now
programme.desc: Adrienne Murray meets the team using tech to preserve a historic warship in Sweden. Andrew Rogers has the highlights from the Esports World Cup in Paris. Suranjana Tewari heads behind the scenes of a driverless taxi service in Beijing. And Ammie Sekhon finds out why medical students are practicing with AI-powered virtual patients.

programme.title: World's Ultimate Adventures
programme.desc: Chef and content creator Julie Lin is on a Turkish adventure - combining her passion for food with history. Travelling through the south east, known as the gastronomic heart, she first stops in the city of Gazianetep - world famous for its baklava. Julie uncovers what makes this delicacy and the locally grown pistachios inside it so special. Heading further east, she visits the Neolithic site of Karahan Tepe, a discovery so significant that it is reshaping our understanding of human history. Guided by the archaeological team, Julie explores their latest finds, including what may be the world's oldest kitchen. Her journey ends in Şanlıurfa, cooking with a family keeping traditional recipes alive, discovering the city's signature smoked pepper, and finishing her trip with a vibrant cultural, night-time celebration and an unusual raw-meat dish.

programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: Inside China's EV Revolution
programme.desc: At a time of heightened geopolitical conflict and uncertainty, soaring fuel costs are driving up demand for electric vehicles around the world. Chinese EV's are leading the way. In the span of a decade, China's electric vehicles sector has gone from fledgling industry to automotive powerhouse, challenging some the world's top automakers on their home ground. We examine how China transformed into the world's leading manufacturer of green energy cars, from innovations in battery technology to the concept of a smartphone on wheels, and ultimately what lies ahead for the future of transportation.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: For years, YouTube was largely seen as the home of creators who built their audiences online. But increasingly it's becoming a destination for established TV presenters too. James May, best known for Top Gear and The Grand Tour, joins Katie Razzall alongside producer Lucy Brown to discuss building their YouTube channel, Planet Gin. Holly Graham, chief commercial officer at Little Dot Studios, explains what it takes to build a successful YouTube brand and whether television success translates online. The Times's chief sports reporter Martyn Ziegler revealed that FIFA president Gianni Infantino had been exploring plans to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Martyn explains how he broke the story, while Tariq Panja, global sports correspondent at The New York Times, discusses the growing role of investigative journalism in football. The resignation of University of Cambridge professor Jason Arday has become one of the biggest stories in British academia. Jack Grove, investigations editor at Times Higher Education, explains how he first uncovered concerns about Arday and why legal threats prevented publication at the time.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: On the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, Dwayne Fields travels across the USA, exploring how the document's famous promise - the pursuit of happiness - is being lived today. In part one of two, Dwayne finds out how the Great Migration has impacted Chicago, tries America's highest zip line in Colorado before saddling up to see how tourism has transformed the lives of Utah's iconic cowboys.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon continues on the penultimate day of the European Athletics Championships with the long jump and javelin. Meanwhile, the fastest woman in Europe this season over 1,500m, Georgia Hunter Bell, is in action in qualifying for Sunday’s final alongside 2022 champion Laura Muir. The sprint relay teams also take to the track for the first time in the heats. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion dives into the glamorous past of Saltdean Lido, the only Grade II listed coastal lido in the UK. The building was designed in the 1930s in the streamline moderne architectural style. Christina learns how the building epitomised the sleek art deco look and captured the carefree spirit of the era. In Kingston upon Thames, the teams scour an antiques centre in search of bargains under the guidance of their experts, John Cameron and Richard Madley, in the hope that they will make a profit at auction in Cranbrook, where Raj Bisram is wielding his gavel.

programme.title: Chicken Run
programme.desc: Award-winning animation. Despite many failed attempts, Ginger the hen is convinced that escape is possible from terrible Tweedy Farm. When a cocky rooster called Rocky flies into the lives of the chickens, she hopes her dream of freedom might finally come true. Featuring the voices of Mel Gibson (Rocky), Julia Sawalha (Ginger), Miranda Richardson (Mrs Tweedy), Jane Horrocks (Babs), Lynn Ferguson (Mac), Imelda Staunton (Bunty), Benjamin Whitrow (Fowler), Anthony Haygarth (Mr Tweedy), Timothy Spall (Nick) and Phil Daniels (Fletcher).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Steve Brown marvels at the spectacular scenery on offer in Scotland's Perth and Kinross and beyond as he helps a couple with three children from a city in Essex find their dream home in the countryside. They need a big garden, good transport links and want to be within half an hour of a rugby club.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Chris are in Penarth to transform Hannah and Gemma’s overgrown and unloved plot into a Tulum jungle bar garden. They are hoping for a sophisticated and exotic space that echoes some of their travels, particularly their trips to Mexico. Can the Garden Rescue team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: The Hit List
programme.desc: Competing this week are best friends Sophie and Lauren from Liverpool, married couple Jack and Ashleigh from Swansea, and father-in-law and son-in-law Glen and Rob from Pontefract. With big hits and big pressure, who will hit the right note and make it to the final chart rundown?

programme.title: Alan Carr's Picture Slam
programme.desc: Comedian Alan Carr hosts the fun and frantic quiz show where every question is a picture and every picture is worth cash. They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are Ian and Liz, a couple from Stoke-on-Trent, friends Arif and Kausar from London, and Rachel and Connor, two friends from Leeds. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night of action on the penultimate day of the European Athletics Championships, with nine new champions crowned in Birmingham. The final event of the heptathlon, the 800m, kicks off a busy evening session. There are medal chances in the women’s high jump for Morgan Lake and in the women’s 400 metres for Amber Anning, while the men’s 1,500 metres sees Jake Wightman trying to add European gold to his world silver. The night concludes with the men's and women’s sprint relay finals. Gabby Logan leads the coverage and is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night of action on the penultimate day of the European Athletics Championships, with nine new champions crowned in Birmingham. programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night of action on the penultimate day of the European Athletics Championships, with nine new champions crowned in Birmingham. The final event of the heptathlon, the 800m, kicks off a busy evening session. There are medal chances in the women’s high jump for Morgan Lake and in the women’s 400 metres for Amber Anning, while the men’s 1,500 metres sees Jake Wightman trying to add European gold to his world silver. The night concludes with the men's and women’s sprint relay finals. Gabby Logan leads the coverage and is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon continues on the penultimate day of the European Athletics Championships with the long jump and javelin. Meanwhile, the fastest woman in Europe this season over 1,500m, Georgia Hunter Bell, is in action in qualifying for Sunday’s final alongside 2022 champion Laura Muir. The sprint relay teams also take to the track for the first time in the heats. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion dives into the glamorous past of Saltdean Lido, the only Grade II listed coastal lido in the UK. The building was designed in the 1930s in the streamline moderne architectural style. Christina learns how the building epitomised the sleek art deco look and captured the carefree spirit of the era. In Kingston upon Thames, the teams scour an antiques centre in search of bargains under the guidance of their experts, John Cameron and Richard Madley, in the hope that they will make a profit at auction in Cranbrook, where Raj Bisram is wielding his gavel.

programme.desc: Award-winning animation. Despite many failed attempts, Ginger the hen is convinced that escape is possible from terrible Tweedy Farm. When a cocky rooster called Rocky flies into the lives of the chickens, she hopes her dream of freedom might finally come true. Featuring the voices of Mel Gibson (Rocky), Julia Sawalha (Ginger), Miranda Richardson (Mrs Tweedy), Jane Horrocks (Babs), Lynn Ferguson (Mac), Imelda Staunton (Bunty), Benjamin Whitrow (Fowler), Anthony Haygarth (Mr Tweedy), Timothy Spall (Nick) and Phil Daniels (Fletcher).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Steve Brown marvels at the spectacular scenery on offer in Scotland's Perth and Kinross and beyond as he helps a couple with three children from a city in Essex find their dream home in the countryside. They need a big garden, good transport links and want to be within half an hour of a rugby club.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Chris are in Penarth to transform Hannah and Gemma’s overgrown and unloved plot into a Tulum jungle bar garden. They are hoping for a sophisticated and exotic space that echoes some of their travels, particularly their trips to Mexico. Can the Garden Rescue team achieve all this on a £5,000 budget?

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Look North (East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire)
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire.

programme.title: BBC Weather
programme.desc: The latest weather forecast.

programme.title: The Hit List
programme.desc: Competing this week are best friends Sophie and Lauren from Liverpool, married couple Jack and Ashleigh from Swansea, and father-in-law and son-in-law Glen and Rob from Pontefract. With big hits and big pressure, who will hit the right note and make it to the final chart rundown?

programme.title: Alan Carr's Picture Slam
programme.desc: Comedian Alan Carr hosts the fun and frantic quiz show where every question is a picture and every picture is worth cash. They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are Ian and Liz, a couple from Stoke-on-Trent, friends Arif and Kausar from London, and Rachel and Connor, two friends from Leeds. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night of action on the penultimate day of the European Athletics Championships, with nine new champions crowned in Birmingham. The final event of the heptathlon, the 800m, kicks off a busy evening session. There are medal chances in the women’s high jump for Morgan Lake and in the women’s 400 metres for Amber Anning, while the men’s 1,500 metres sees Jake Wightman trying to add European gold to his world silver. The night concludes with the men's and women’s sprint relay finals. Gabby Logan leads the coverage and is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: Mission: Impossible
programme.desc: When a crucial mission goes wrong, spy Ethan Hunt finds himself out on a limb and under suspicion. Taking the law into his own hands, he races to clear his name and expose the real traitor.

programme.title: Spider-Man: Far from Home
programme.desc: Dodging responsibilities, Peter Parker takes a school trip to Europe but lands in monstrous trouble. Nick Fury expects Spider-Man to step up and help prevent further disaster, alongside a newly arrived hero, but the teen from Queens doubts himself.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: All the weekend national, UK-wide and international news on Saturday evening at 7.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team are in Alloa, Scotland’s smallest county, hoping to revive Alloa Co-op Bowling Club’s faded and warped sign in their centenary year. Meanwhile, Dom delivers Steve a 19th-century regulator clock from the Hebrides that has a ghostly connection, and Will heads north to Rothes to learn the fiery, and very loud, craft behind forging traditional copper stills for the multibillion-dollar whisky industry.

programme.title: The Town That Floored the World
programme.desc: How did the Scottish east coast port town of Kirkcaldy become the world centre for linoleum? The Town That Floored the World traces the history of that “magic material” to its origins in the mid 19th century, and tells how one town built its fortunes on its manufacture. Current and former linoleum workers, and Kirkcaldy bairns including crime writer Val McDermid, share their stories of a life in flooring. Lino’s role in high art and design is also traced. Narrated by John Sessions.

programme.title: Murder Trial
programme.desc: In 2024, the body of 65-year-old groundsman Brian Low is discovered on a country track in rural Aberfeldy, his beloved black labrador Millie by his side. Police assume that Brian has suffered a medical episode, but six days later, the post-mortem reveals the shocking truth - Brian has been shot dead. His former colleague and gamekeeper on the estate where he worked, David Campbell, now stands trial for his murder. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased. The prosecution builds a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence while working to convince the jury that he is guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

programme.title: The Fringe, Fame and Me
programme.desc: The story of how a small Scottish arts festival that began in 1947 became a national institution that has seen new stars forged, careers made and dreams dashed. Told by the stars who first found fame at the Edinburgh Fringe, this is the inside story of what it takes to make a name here - from those who enjoyed overnight success to those who slogged for years to make it. Through their triumphs, favourite jokes and sometimes painful failures, we discover a hidden history of British comedy, revealing how the gags we find funny and the comedians we love reflect our changing culture.

programme.title: Jules and Greg's Wild Swim
programme.desc: Celebrity couple Julie Wilson Nimmo and Greg Hemphill share their passion for wild outdoor swimming in Scotland and give us an unprecedented insight into their lives as a married couple. This week, Jules and Greg are in Glasgow and Edinburgh, exploring Scotland’s urban cold-water locations.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: With a mutilated boy still missing, Shepherd and Roach are desperate to get some information out of Donna before it’s too late. Meanwhile, Barbara and Elise attend an infamous St Stephens college party to reclaim Barbara’s reputation and kick-start Elise’s. But things go off course when a visitor from Barbara’s past threatens to derail everything.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: As Barbara comes to terms with her past trauma at a university group therapy session, Elise is doing her best to be a supportive friend while also stopping the archaeology club from digging up evidence linking them to the night of the murder. Meanwhile, the war between the men's rights activists and the radical feminists reaches its violent crescendo.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: Barbara is MIA, while Elise packs her bags for home. But when they discover that the killer is planning the biggest murder yet, the girls must decide if they can stop them for good.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Twenty-five-year-old Mancunian Tyler is a self-confessed serial dater who treats dating like a sport and goes on five or six dates a week. She’s rude and sarcastic, rambles on about herself, gets bored easily and doesn’t stay focused on her dates. Best mate Yazmine is sick of hearing about Tyler’s dating disasters. Tyler needs help, so Yazmine calls on Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to kick-start an intervention. Oloni pulls Tyler up on her catastrophic dating habits and delivers some tough truths as she and Tyler watch frank video feedback from friends and exes to prove to Tyler that there needs to be a change. Oloni has her job cut out with this one and sets Tyler up on three challenge dates as she and Yazmine watch on. Tyler insists her ideal date is the male version of herself, but will the male ‘Tyler’ be the perfect match for this feisty female?

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: Mervin begrudgingly embraces island life and agrees to watch a local women’s football game with the team. But half-time sees a bloody discovery when the star player is found dead in the locker rooms with a fatal bullet wound. The team are left perplexed when it becomes clear that the only way to access the changing rooms is via the pitch - and no-one in the crowd saw anything. So, how did the killer slip through the net? As Mervin feels the pressure from Selwyn over a murder that took place right under their noses, Naomi is at a crossroads when someone from her past turns up on the island.

programme.desc: When Dad runs out of marmalade, Big Lizard shows Cosima a plant that's growing Proximan oranges. The leaves turn out to be giant bugs, who aren't happy about sharing their fruit!

programme.desc: Weasy has forgotten the ducklings' birthday and quickly makes them something - but it falls apart. The ducklings are sad when they realise he forgot - they will have to find their own present.

programme.desc: Ult leaves the Brave Olivine after an argument with Roy.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: Excitement builds as Musa’s concert in Magixia approaches, but her nerves skyrocket when a mysterious agent shows interest.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Malory Towers
programme.desc: Gwen is shocked into drastic action when her father refuses to sign her application to finishing school. Meanwhile, Darrell and Felicity fall out during the North Tower Spelling Bee.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As the drought takes its toll on Longmeadow, Monty takes stock of his garden and has a radical rethink about what he should be growing in the future. With this in mind, he takes cuttings of some drought-resistant plants as a way of saving money. There is also a rambling rose in desperate need of a haircut and lots of produce to harvest in the veg garden, so as always, there is plenty to be getting on with. Frances Tophill visits the picturesque village of Clovelly in north Devon, where gardening on a clifftop is not without its challenges. And in Norfolk, Adam Frost explores a walled kitchen garden steeped in history but planted with a modern eye. On the Isle of Wight, a couple tell the incredible story of how they’ve reimagined the Victorian garden of the poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson, while a gardener in East Anglia showcases his love of naturalistic planting.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Brian Cunningham delve into the mailbox to tackle a host of viewers’ questions sent in from around the country. Even though we are well into the growing season, the pair start a major new project as they launch a makeover of a Beechgrove area known as the Crooked Garden. One of the first parts of that revamp is the creation of a stumpery, a growing technique based on an old tree and planted with a range of ferns. George has details on how to feed a cherry tree, Brian is back in the 8x6 greenhouse, and there is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt serves up a delicious summer feast from some of your favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Ben Lippett dishes up his baked paprika cod with a chorizo and pea dressing, which pairs perfectly with his mustardy bean salad. Karan Gokani brings his iconic hoppers, served with a spicy, fragrant black pork curry. Georgina Hayden makes vine leaf cake centrepieces filled with spiced pork, tomatoes and rice, served with thick Greek yogurt and plenty of fresh herbs. Olia Hercules presents soft berry buns filled with the best of seasonal fruit. Carmen O’Neal gives afternoon tea a cocktail glow-up, and Laura Whitmore tucks into either her food heaven, seafood linguine, or her food hell, a blooming onion. Meanwhile, Rick Stein goes on a heather honey hunt in the Scottish Highlands, and the Hairy Bikers get a taste of the Corsican holy trinity.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: Wildlife broadcaster Liz Bonnin has travelled the world, but Clare on Ireland's west coast keeps calling her back. Its wild landscape and biodiversity captivated her as a teenager, and Anna is eager to explore. Liz introduces Anna to those preserving Ireland's food culture by growing heritage fruits and vegetables. In Burren National Park, Liz reflects on her initial lack of love for Irish food, but Anna takes her to an award-winning goat cheesemaker to change her mind.

programme.title: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
programme.desc: With plenty of deceptively easy recipes and fantastic tips, Lorraine Pascale shows people with no kitchen confidence how to pull off an impressive meal for friends and family. In this episode she helps 52-year-old builder Tony Sartori, who has never cooked a meal in his life, to master a delicious Mediterranean-inspired menu which includes a grilled peach and burrata salad, crispy salmon with polenta chips and grilled asparagus, and a dessert with real wow factor.

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Cooking
programme.desc: Nigel Slater continues his exploration of brilliant culinary combinations, this episode he's turning his attention to texture. Success in the kitchen isn't just about tastes and flavours - contrasting textures can really lift a dish. He'll be making a classic savoury pie with a puff pastry crust, and will be putting traditional pizza ingredients together in a new way to make an entirely original dish. Nigel also travels to Brighton to meet a couple who have their own seafront smokery, who'll be showing him a soft and crisp recipe of their own.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Gymnastics: European Championships
programme.desc: Coverage of the women's apparatus finals from the 2026 European Gymnastics Championships in Zagreb, Croatia.

programme.title: Superman III
programme.desc: A high school reunion puts Clark Kent back in touch with an old sweetheart as a megalomaniac plots to use a bumbling computer genius to control a technology so powerful even Superman cannot compete.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents an emotional night at the Royal Albert Hall celebrating 40 years of Paul Simon's groundbreaking album. Ladysmith Black Mambazo, who featured prominently on the album, are joined by James Bay, Laura Mvula and others on the Royal Albert Hall stage to perform hits like You Can Call Me Al, Diamonds on the Soles of Her Shoes and The Boy in the Bubble.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: A veritable who’s who of music graced the Top of the Pops studio in 2003, including Sugababes, Coldplay, OutKast, Panjabi MC, Madonna and Black Eyed Peas, as well as Beyoncé’s first solo single.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: The story of 2003, a year of wall-to-wall bangers where nobody was sticking to the rules. With contributions from artists including Matt Willis, Justin Hawkins, Panjabi MC and Peter Doherty.

programme.title: Beyoncé at the BBC
programme.desc: To celebrate Beyoncé reaching her 40th birthday, this gift to her fans takes a trip through the archives for a selection of the best of Queen Bey at the BBC. The collection shows why we are all Crazy in Love with her and features several iconic live performances, with hits like Naughty Girl, Irreplaceable and of course Single Ladies, underlining how she has become one of the biggest musical stars on the planet.

programme.title: Glastonbury
programme.desc: Sugababes performing at the 2024 Glastonbury Festival.

programme.title: The Graduate
programme.desc: Benjamin Braddock is a shy, aimless college graduate. His well-to-do parents and their friends welcome him home with great fanfare, but he feels listless, lacks ambition and can't share their enthusiasm. When his parents' friend Mrs Robinson takes an interest in him, it kick-starts an unusual summer.

Olia Hercules presents soft berry buns filled with the best of seasonal fruit. Carmen O’Neal gives afternoon tea a cocktail glow-up, and Laura Whitmore tucks into either her food heaven, seafood linguine, or her food hell, a blooming onion. Meanwhile, Rick Stein goes on a heather honey hunt in the Scottish Highlands, and the Hairy Bikers get a taste of the Corsican holy trinity.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour

programme.title: Bing

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Diesel is a hearing dog for his teenage owner, Rayane, who is deaf. This means he doesn’t hear everything. Diesel is trained to listen out for important sounds that Rayane might miss. Diesel has a busy day ahead. First, he has to filter out all the sounds in the busy park to help Rayane find his friends Grace and Karim and the rest of his teammates at the start line. Then, he has to listen for the klaxon so he can let Rayane know the race is starting. He doesn’t want him to get left behind! Rayane’s football coach uses British Sign Language to communicate the rules of the race to the runners before they set off. Diesel has to run alongside Rayane and alert him to any danger or to anyone trying to get past. Karim is leading the field until he takes a wrong turn – and Rayane and Diesel set off in hot pursuit. Can they catch their friend and help him finish the race?

programme.desc: Diesel is a hearing dog for his teenage owner, Rayane, who is deaf. This means he doesn’t hear everything. Diesel is trained to listen out for important sounds that Rayane might miss. Diesel is Rayane’s ears. Together, they’re unstoppable! Diesel and Rayane are off to the park, where their football team are doing a sponsored fun run to raise the funds for a new kit. Diesel has a busy day ahead. First, he has to filter out all the sounds in the busy park to help Rayane find his friends Grace and Karim and the rest of his teammates at the start line. Then, he has to listen for the klaxon so he can let Rayane know the race is starting. He doesn’t want him to get left behind! Rayane’s football coach uses British Sign Language to communicate the rules of the race to the runners before they set off. Diesel has to run alongside Rayane and alert him to any danger or to anyone trying to get past. Karim is leading the field until he takes a wrong turn – and Rayane and Diesel set off in hot pursuit. Can they catch their friend and help him finish the race?

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Evie’s ball has gone into a hedge that eats balls! Taran is determined to get it back, so he and Theo attempt the impossible: retrieving the ball from the Hungry Hedge.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: When Gadabout and Pearl lose the cure for Madam Dragon’s missing flame, Zog helps them work together to assist his former teacher.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Bluey and Bingo visit Grandad, he takes them on an adventure into the bush.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Steve and Aneeshwar help the keepers by setting up a new toy in the tigers' enclosure. They see what makes the tiger such an incredible predator. Next, they get to hold an animal called a leaf insect and see how it looks just like a plant. Steve and Aneeshwar then reveal the wild connection between these two very different animals.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the exceptional painter Spinach creating Kiwi’s portrait, if Kiwi can keep still.

programme.title: Tish Tash
programme.desc: The family all go to the park to visit the playground, and to Tish's disappointment, there are already kids on the new climbing frame. Tish hides in fear of the kids and imagines them as aliens. Tash tells them she's a space mechanic and can fix their ship.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: The friends are excited to stay with Marvin at the Bat Cave - it's going to be so much fun! When they get to the cave, the bats are sound asleep, hibernating for the winter. The friends must be very quiet so they don't wake them up - but it's difficult to keep quiet when everyone's playing together.

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: ­Rain is forecast in Fluffytown, but Love Monster is excited because his friends are coming round for an indoor activity day. They're going to knit onesies, drink hot chocolate and build a pillow fort! But when the weather turns out to be glorious, Love Monster's friends want to play outside instead. Eventually Love Monster is convinced to join them but when he does, it rains! Disappointed, his friends start to head back inside, but Love Monster says they can do his indoor activities outdoors!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Octo-alert! Lots of things in Numberland have been split into halves, thirds and four equal parts. There’s only one block naughty enough to cause such mischief - it’s Octonaughty. Octoblock catches up with Octonaughty in The Museum of Numbers as he causes havoc with his new invention, the Fractionator. Octonaughty is splitting things into equal parts to try to steal the Golden Infinity, but how can Octoblock save the day when Octonaughty has the power to split him into four equal parts?

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: The Colourblocks discover a series of colour wheels. But where should they sit on them? Learn which colours go next to each other with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button discover dental floss and plan an exciting tug-of-war showdown.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella tries to brush Lift’s teeth, but it is too tickly - can the Playtimers help? This gives Hettie an idea for a dance, the Brush Boogie!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Sonny finds an old musical safe, which only opens with the right musical code. With Yukee’s help, Sonny tries every tune he can think of, but none opens the box – until the answer appears in a very unexpected place!

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children plant sunflower seeds in decorated pots to grow beautiful flowers, learn British Sign Language signs for garden, grow and pretty, then sing and sign Mary, Mary, Quite Contrary.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick and Norman are going to an animal fancy dress party but what animal will Nick go as?

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: After Pancake saves him from a mishap, Flutter vows to repay the debt. But his risk-averse behaviour drives Pan to distraction until a real emergency allows the debt to be repaid.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Gadabout and Pearl need Zog's help to catch a stink beetle for an urgent cure. Little do they know, Zog has become a taxi for the gnomes.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Finn puts on a magic show at the bakery and wants to do it all by himself. It goes well - until he gets stuck. Rafi secretly makes a wish, and suddenly his hat is full of bunnies! The crowd laughs, but Finn is upset that the show isn’t his anymore. With Ruby’s help, they use carrot cake to guide the bunnies back into the hat. When the wish ends, Finn finishes the show on his own. He proves he can shine, and Rafi realises that friends sometimes need space to do things their own way.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Bluey and Bingo visit Grandad, he takes them on an adventure into the bush.

programme.title: Nikhil & Jay
programme.desc: When Nikhil and Jay break Nana’s lollipop stick, they decide to make her a new one. But how can they make sure Nana likes it?

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. The librarian has lost his big reference book and Sarah thinks her toy periscope might help with the search.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Lola doesn't like the hat that Lotta gives her. It's itchy and it has dangly bits. Even Soren Lorenson, Lola's imaginary friend, thinks it wouldn't be too bad if she lost the hat by accident. It's only when she really does lose it that Lola realises her friendship with Lotta is more important.

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: Moon Baby, Pepi Nana and all the friends find a toy roundabout has been left in the Toy House. Each chooses a vehicle to ride in and they have a race. Mr Onion thinks his very slow Bumparoller will be last, but he’s in for a surprise…

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa measure things that are bigger and smaller. A ladybird is much smaller than MeMo and BaBa. At Play Time, they choose a magnifier and use it to look at the ladybird. The ladybird looks much bigger! They show the magnifier to the Yummies and use it to look at their snack. The tiny pea looks enormous. On the Lullaby Lake, they don’t need anything to make Elewhale look bigger.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. Everybody is running about in the garden so much that Makka Pakka can't wash faces. After a lot of fun and chasing, they all come together and Makka Pakka succeeds in his task.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: In our first case of this episode, Mark Thorpe has always wondered about the identity of the baby in the photo by his late mum's bed, an image she also had tattooed on her arm, since he was a little boy - when he was older, Mark's mum revealed that she'd had a son before him who was placed for adoption, and now he yearns to find his older brother. In our second case, Jane Lewis was taken into foster care when she was 11 days old - it was hoped that Jane's mother would one day return to look after Jane, but she never did and Jane remained in care for the whole of her childhood. Jane recently discovered that her mother had three other children - brothers of which two who were in care and one who was adopted - and now she wants to find them.

programme.title: Boris Karloff: The Man Behind
programme.desc: the Monster. 2021. Documentary. Directed by Thomas Hamilton. Features Ron Perlman, Guillermo del Toro. A look at the life and legacy of Boris Karloff, and the history of the genre he personified.

programme.title: The Vise
programme.desc: The Gamblers. 1954. Stars Ron Randell, Martin Benson & Thea Gregory. June Belmont is invited by Carlos Rodrigues to join the roulette table. June brings Carlos some luck so they become partners. [S]

programme.title: The Detectives
programme.desc: Tobey's Place. Captain Matt Holbrook (Robert Taylor) leads a squad of brave and tough detectives tackling crime. Also Stars: Tige Andrews, Russell Thorson, Adam West

programme.title: Colonel March Investigates
programme.desc: 1953. Crime drama starring Boris Karloff, Joan Sims and Richard Wattis. Colonel March runs the Scotland Yard office for the Department of Queer Complaints and investigates 3 strange crimes. [S]

programme.title: Runaround
programme.desc: 1981. Presented by Mike Reid. Prizes include a badminton set, a cuddly bear and a selection of construction kits. This episode features a Vintage police car and Quasar motorcycle.

programme.title: Legend of the Hidden City
programme.desc: 1997. Stars Brendan Pollecutt, Fezile Mpela & Robert Finlayson. Morgan and Ram engage in mortal combat. Dean must choose between Kama and Nina.

programme.title: William Tell
programme.desc: The Assassins. 1958. Stars Conrad Phillips, Willoughby Goddard & Jennifer Jayne. Swiss collaborators, arrested by Gessler for murder, are given a chance to save their necks from the noose. [S]

programme.title: Batman
programme.desc: The Great Train Robbery. 1968. Stars Adam West, Burt Ward & Yvonne Craig. After his previous battle with the Terrific Trio, Shame now has Batgirl as a hostage. [S]

programme.title: Hawkeye & the Last of the Mohicans
programme.desc: Way Station. 1957. Directed by Sam Newfield. Stars John Hart, Lon Chaney Jr & James Doohan. The daughter of Mingo Chief Nocona is desired by two warring tribesmen. [S]

programme.title: Captain Scarlet and the Mysterons
programme.desc: Expo 2068. 1968. Stars Gary Files, Cy Grant & Sylvia Anderson. The Mysterons get their hands on a truck carrying an atomic core reactor and they plan to strike the Atlantic Seaboard. [S]

programme.title: Supercar
programme.desc: Amazonian Adventure. 1961. Stars David Graham, George Murcell & Graydon Gould. Mike goes on a dangerous mission to South America using Supercar to locate a plant needed to save Mitch's life. [S]

programme.title: The Buccaneers
programme.desc: The Decoy. 1957. Stars Robert Shaw, Virginia Maskell & Marne Maitland. Whilst Tempest sails to Charleston, he encounters a strange woman alone in a boat at sea who tells him a peculiar story. [S]

programme.title: The Adventures of Robin Hood
programme.desc: The Shell Game. 1957. Stars Richard Greene, Sam Kydd & Irene Handl. Robin enlists the help of a thief to obtain royal jewels for King Richard, but Little John is suspicious of the newcomer. [S]

programme.title: The Great Van Robbery
programme.desc: 1959. Crime Drama. Director: Max Varnel. Stars Denis Shaw, Kay Callard & Tony Quinn. An Interpol detective pursues a dangerous thief who has placed his loot into a bank account in Rio de Janeiro. [S]

programme.title: The Four Feathers (1939)
programme.desc: 1939. Adventure. Director: Zoltan Korda. Stars John Clements, Ralph Richardson & C. Aubrey Smith. A British officer seeks to redeem his cowardice 'feathers' by secretly aiding his former comrades. [S]

programme.title: Whiplash
programme.desc: The Haunted Valley. 1961. Stars Peter Graves, Bettina Welch & Ron Whelan. Cobb searches for a friend who told him of a secret source of water in the Australian interior but finds the man dead. [S]

programme.title: Gift Horse
programme.desc: 1952. Director: Compton Bennett. Stars Trevor Howard, Richard Attenborough, Sonny Tufts. In 1940, the Captain of an old Royal Navy destroyer struggles with his crew, as well as the Nazis. [S]

programme.title: Look At Life Over and Under
programme.desc: 1960. We take a look at modern bridge building in Britain. Thousands of new bridges of all shapes and sizes are being constructed all over the country to keep up with the new roads programme.

programme.title: Dick Turpin
programme.desc: The Turncoat. 1979. Stars Richard O'Sullivan, David Daker & Forbes Collins. Spiker is ambushed whilst carrying a letter for Sir John Glutton, who then forces Dick Turpin to recover the message. [S]

programme.title: Maigret
programme.desc: My Friend The Inspector. 1960. Stars Rupert Davies, Ewen Solo & Marian Spencer. A savage murder on the Mediterranean island of Porquerolles provides a change of scene for Inspector Maigret. [S]

programme.title: The Duchess of Duke Street
programme.desc: The Patriots. 1977. Stars Gemma Jones, Alan Gifford & Derek Farr. Louisa becomes concerned when a government official informs her that the hotel is hosting spies. [S]

programme.title: Francis Durbridge's Melissa
programme.desc: Part 3. 1974. Stars Peter Barkworth, Ronald Fraiser & Joan Benham. Guy Foster sets a trap for the killer, talk of a tape recording draws the whole truth out. [S]

programme.title: Turn The Key Softly
programme.desc: 1953. Drama. Director: Jack Lee. Stars Yvonne Mitchell, Joan Collins, Kathleen Harrison. Three women are released from Holloway prison on the same morning into the bustle of post-war London. [S]

programme.title: EuroTrash
programme.desc: 1997. Tonight, EuroTrash gets a visit from the brilliant French dancer and singer Lova Moor but not before we take a look at a Russian Hippy University!

programme.title: Fortean TV
programme.desc: 1997. Hosted by Reverend Lionel Fanthorpe. Tonight, take to the air with a man who can fly like a bird, reveal how leeches are making a medical come back and look for the lost city of Atlantis.

programme.title: One Step Beyond
programme.desc: Image of Death. 1959. Starring: Doris Dowling & John Wengraf. An inspector becomes suspicious when a stain on the wall shows to be an image of the face of the Marquis' dead wife. [S]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. Our coasts have always been an extreme environment to raise a family, but the challenges of parenthood are exacerbated with warming seas - forming earlier than ever before, a hurricane catches a flamingo colony while their chicks are still on the nest. Rain, wind and rising sea levels are a triple threat, but these extraordinary birds have begun to adapt to the new extremes by extending their breeding window and given those who lost their chicks a second chance - meanwhile, a sea otter mum faces a huge winter storm in California and a clownfish on the Great Barrier Reef witnesses her anemone home bleach. However, the clownfish is not ready to give up and sets about reviving it - perhaps most remarkable of all, though, is a little anole lizard that clings on for dear life during a hurricane, surviving as those with the longest toes are the species most able to keep their grip.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: In our first case of this episode, Mark Thorpe has always wondered about the identity of the baby in the photo by his late mum's bed, an image she also had tattooed on her arm, since he was a little boy - when he was older, Mark's mum revealed that she'd had a son before him who was placed for adoption, and now he yearns to find his older brother. In our second case, Jane Lewis was taken into foster care when she was 11 days old - it was hoped that Jane's mother would one day return to look after Jane, but she never did and Jane remained in care for the whole of her childhood. Jane recently discovered that her mother had three other children - brothers of which two who were in care and one who was adopted - and now she wants to find them.
